fields.features_heading: What the Front Desk Gets Back
fields.features_subheading: Each signed consent comes back with the details a clipboard copy leaves out.
fields.feature_1:
Signed on a phone before the visit starts

Send the link with the appointment reminder, or post a code at the front window. Patients read and sign on their own phone, and the signature lands on their record with the time.
fields.feature_2:
The exact wording each patient agreed to

Number each version of your consent text. Every signed record keeps that number. A signature from March still points to March's wording after you rewrite a clause in May.
fields.feature_3:
Privacy notice receipt in the same link

Put the notice of privacy practices before the signature and ask the patient to confirm they received it. The acknowledgment is dated and saved with the consent as one record.
fields.feature_4:
Each treatment accepted or declined

List the treatments your consent covers, such as injections or manual therapy. A patient can say no to one and sign for the rest, and the declined item shows on the schedule.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts that carry a link, not the answers

Send an email or Slack message when a form is in. The alert says a consent was signed and links to the record, and every answer stays in a database you own, never in the message.
fields.feature_6:
Code to run inside your own systems

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Run the consent form inside your patient portal or intake app, and keep editing it there without a rebuild from scratch.

fields.tab_content_1:
Who is still unsigned at 8:40 a.m.

Bellcrest Urgent Care posts a code at its check-in window, and patients sign version 3 of its consent from a waiting room chair. At 8:40 a.m. the front desk's Slack channel gets a count, 11 of 12 morning patients signed, and a link to the list. No names go in the message. The last patient signs on the desk tablet.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every intake signed before the first hour

Willow Street Counseling sends its consent with the intake link 2 days before a client's first session. The client initials the 24-hour cancellation policy and the limits of confidentiality, then signs. The therapist gets an email that a consent form is in, with a link to the record and nothing else.
fields.tab_content_3:
No dry needling, and the therapist sees it

Wrenwood Physical Therapy lists four treatments on its consent, and a new patient answers each one before she signs. Nadia Holm accepts 3 of 4 and declines dry needling. Her 10:30 a.m. slot on the therapist's schedule shows the declined technique. Nobody reaches for the needles at her first visit.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every 12 months, by the clinic's own rule

Amberline Family Medicine decided that patients re-sign its consent once a year. When a patient books, the app checks the date of the last signature on file. Paul Becker's is 13 months old, and the current wording, version 4, goes to him by email before the visit. He signs it at 9:05 a.m., before he reaches the front desk.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Consent to Treat Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a consent to treat form patients sign online before the visit, with each version of the wording on record.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Start from the consent you use now
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Number each version of the wording
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Keep routine care on this form
fields.howto_step_1_des: Paste your current paper consent into the prompt, one clause at a time. Emergent builds each clause as a short section a patient reads on a phone, with the signature at the end. Keep the wording your clinic has already approved.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Call the first text version 1 and raise the number whenever a clause changes. The app stores that number on every signature. Open any patient's record and it shows the exact words they read, even after three rewrites.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Show your notice of privacy practices on its own screen, followed by a box the patient checks to confirm receipt. The front desk then gets the acknowledgment and the consent from one link, not two sheets to file.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide what this general consent covers, such as exams and lab draws. Give a procedure with real risks its own consent, written with the clinician who performs it. List the routine items one per line so each can be declined.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Pick when the link goes out
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose the moment each patient gets the form. Booked visits can carry it in the confirmation email 2 days ahead. Walk-in clinics can post a code at the window, and the waiting room becomes the place where patients sign.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set how long a signature stays current
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose the interval your clinic will use, for example 12 months, and write it into the prompt as a rule. Any patient whose signature is older than that gets the current version to sign ahead of the next appointment.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run it with five real check-ins
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sign the form yourself on a phone first. Then run it with five patients at the front desk and read the records they produce. Rewrite any clause that drew a question, and raise the version number before it goes live.

faq_plan.q: What is a consent to treat form?
faq_plan.ref: What is a consent to treat form?

prov.original: What is a consent to treat form?

faq_plan.a: It is the general consent a patient signs before care starts, so the practice may examine and treat them. Collect it ahead of the first visit and file the signed copy in the patient's record.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a consent to treat form?
faq_plan.a: Describe the consent you use now to Emergent's AI form builder, clause by clause, and name who should hear when one is signed. Emergent builds the form with its signature step, plus the database behind it. Change any part later by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: What sections go on a consent for treatment form?
faq_plan.a: Start with what the practice may do: the exams, tests, and routine treatment the consent covers. Add a line on saying no, since patients also have the right to refuse treatment, in the Merck Manual's words. Finish with the privacy notice acknowledgment and a dated signature.

faq_plan.q: How is a consent to treat form different from what a tattoo studio has clients sign?
faq_plan.a: One covers medical care at a practice, and the other covers a service at a studio. A tattoo consent form checks each client's age and photo ID before the work starts. The build is alike: sections the person reads, then a dated signature.

faq_plan.q: How do I add the privacy notice to a consent to treat form?
faq_plan.a: Give the notice its own screen before the signature, with a checkbox for receipt. HIPAA's rule for covered providers who treat patients directly reads: except in an emergency treatment situation, make a good faith effort to obtain a written acknowledgment of receipt of the notice. The notice goes out no later than the date of the first service delivery.

faq_plan.q: Can a consent to treat form let a patient refuse one treatment?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put each covered treatment on its own line with accept and decline choices. Declining one line does not block the signature on the others. The record names the refused line, with the date and the wording version the patient read.

faq_plan.q: When does a procedure need its own form instead of the consent to treat form?
faq_plan.a: When it is invasive or risky. The Merck Manual says express informed consent is always required for those, while routine care is typically treated as implied. An anesthesia consent form, for example, is its own form that records the anesthetic plan and its own signature.

faq_plan.q: How do I track which version of a consent to treat form each patient signed?
faq_plan.a: Number the wording and raise the number with each change, and the app saves it on every signature. Emergent keeps the records in a database you own, and you can list every patient still on an old version before their next visit.

faq_plan.q: Who gets notified when a consent to treat form is signed?
faq_plan.a: The person or channel you name in the prompt: a front desk Slack channel or a therapist's email. Keep the alert to a single line plus a link, and leave the answers in the database. Forms Emergent builds carry no response caps, even on a busy check-in day.

faq_plan.q: Can one consent to treat form cover a clinic that also offers spa services?
faq_plan.a: Use it for the medical care and give each cosmetic service its own form. A waxing consent form asks skin questions for each area booked, which a general consent leaves out. Both forms can save to the same database, and one patient record then holds every signature.

findings.quote: HIPAA's rule for providers who treat patients directly reads: except in an emergency treatment situation, make a good faith effort to obtain a written acknowledgment of receipt of the notice.
findings.issue: The source (45 CFR 164.520(c)(2)) puts this duty on 'a covered health care provider that has a direct treatment relationship with an individual'. The page widens it to every provider who treats patients directly, including practices HIPAA does not cover. YMYL page: the attribution must match the regulation's scope.
findings.fix: Write 'HIPAA's rule for covered providers who treat patients directly reads: ...' (or 'for a covered health care provider with a direct treatment relationship'). Keep the quoted span verbatim.

findings.quote: Sedation is one example: an anesthesia consent form records the plan and its own signature.
findings.issue: Coming right after the Merck sentence, 'Sedation is one example' states as fact that sedation is an invasive or risky intervention needing express informed consent. No spec.domain_sources entry says this, and the cited Merck page does not mention sedation or anesthesia.
findings.fix: Drop the classification and keep the link as a description of a separate form, e.g. 'An anesthesia consent form, for example, is its own form that records the anesthetic plan and its own signature.' Or add a domain source (max 8) that says sedation or anesthesia requires its own informed consent and quote it.
